title: Design audit: ready to test
eyebrow: Built and checked in Chromium (the engine behind Chrome and Edge) · ready for you to test · GitHub issues #281 to #286

short.lead: The design you approved is built. Focus opens on one task. The next step of every area and project is always in view. Roadmap is four columns on a computer. The clipboard is bigger, with the note filling it. Test it on the test copy, which uses sample data and never touches your real tasks.
short.hint: Do the steps in order. Each one says what to press and what you should see.
items: A start page opens with seven buttons, one per screen. Pressing one loads sample data (19 projects, 77 tasks and 2 thoughts) and opens the real app on that tab. Your own tasks are not touched, because the copy runs on a different web address.

Open the page called 'Focus Deck Test Copy: design audit' from the link in my message, on your phone and then on your computer. Press Focus to start. To reset, go back to the start page and press a tab. That puts the sample data back.

items.alt: Focus on a phone: one task on a yellow note, a Done stamp, three plain buttons and four area notes
items.caption: Focus on a phone, as built.

items: Focus shows one task straight away on a yellow note that fills the clipboard, with one Done stamp and three plain buttons. Small coloured notes show the next step of each area on a phone and of each project on a computer.

1. Open Focus and check that a task shows with no question first. 2. Press Not now and check that another task appears. 3. Press Choose… and check that 'Which project?' opens, then press Back. 4. On a phone, tap an area note and check that its projects show, then tap a project note and check that it becomes the big note. 5. Press Done and check that the note is crossed out and 'Next one' appears.

items.alt: Focus on a computer: the clipboard on the left and a note per project on the right
items.caption: Focus on a computer, as built.

items: Roadmap: four columns and the next step
On a computer, Up next, Doing, Review and Done sit side by side. The first Up next task is a yellow note marked 'Next step' on both sizes. A list shows 8 tasks and then a 'Show more' button.

1. On a computer, open Roadmap and check that all four columns show at once. 2. Drag a task from Up next to Doing and check that it stays there. 3. On a phone, check that the yellow Next step note sits above the tabs, and that it stays there when you tap Doing. 4. In a project with more than 8 tasks in a list, press 'Show more' and check that the rest appear.

items.alt: Roadmap on a computer in dark mode with 18 Up next, 65 Doing, 18 Review and 49 Done
items.caption: Roadmap on a computer, dark mode, with a large project.

items: Sort, Review and Triage: one slip, one stamp

The slip fills the clipboard and the edges of the waiting slips show behind it. There is one stamp for the main action and plain buttons for the rest. On a computer the next four slips are listed beside the clipboard.

1. Open Sort and check that the thought fills the clipboard, with 'Sort this one' as the only stamp. 2. Press More and check that the drawer opens. 3. Open Review and check that 'Looks good' is the only stamp and 'More work' is a plain button. 4. On a computer, check that 'After this one' lists what is next. 5. Open Organize, start Triage, and check that 'Yes, do it first' is the only stamp.

items.alt: Review on a computer: one slip on a large clipboard, with After this one listed beside it
items.caption: Review on a computer, as built.

items: Plain buttons carry words; dark mode

The brass handle and the '⋯' tag are now plain buttons that say More (and Sort by on Projects). Every screenshot was also taken in dark mode, which is how I found and fixed an unreadable title and due-date tag.

1. Check that every button you meet has a word on it. 2. Switch your device to dark mode and look at Focus and Roadmap again. Check that the title, the due-date tag on the yellow note and the columns are all readable.

items.alt: Focus on a phone in dark mode with 8 areas: four area notes and an All 8 areas button
items.caption: Focus on a phone, dark mode, with 8 areas.

items: If it all works, the build is ready to become a pull request into main, the version of the app you use.
Reply "QA passed: design audit", or tell me what is wrong and on which screen.

unverified: I could not open the published test copy, because my sandbox cannot reach claude.ai. I served the same files locally instead, and all seven start buttons opened the app on the right tab with no errors
Everything was checked in Chromium at 390 by 844 and 1440 by 900 pixels, not in Safari or Firefox, not on a real phone, and not at the width of your own 2000-pixel window
The 26-project and dark-mode pictures were looked at by eye for Focus and Roadmap only; Sort, Review and Triage in dark mode were measured for fit but not looked at
The print and dyslexia-friendly writing styles were checked by the existing check on the big Focus note, not looked at on the small notes or the Roadmap note
Task details opening beside the Roadmap columns on a computer is covered by the existing checks passing, not looked at by eye
GitHub was not called live; every GitHub call in the checks went to a stand-in
Triage's 'After this one' lists only the rest of its three, so it shows at most two titles
On a computer the Roadmap has no clipboard frame, as in the picture you approved; your answer about the clipboard was applied to Focus, Sort, Review and Organize

wrapup.summary: The design audit is built: Focus, Roadmap, Sort, Review and Triage on a phone and a computer (#282 to #286). All 41 checks in the project's check run pass, 332 unit tests pass, and 40 pictures in light and dark with 8 and 26 projects all fit their window.
wrapup.changing: Changing: the layout of Focus, Roadmap, Sort, Review and Triage. Not changing: the tabs, your data, Projects, Settings and Tidy up.
wrapup.next: After 'QA passed', I open a pull request into main, the version of the app you use. The issues close after the merge.
